correctness.rationale: The symmetry-adjusted two-time energy proves every orbit reaches period at most two. The rim-square identities prove exactly two fixed points and characterize all unchanged-hub two-cycles. For changing hubs, strict inequalities and an exact step-two graph return equation give a bijection with constrained cyclic binary strings. Counting consecutive occupied runs by boundary marking yields the claimed coefficient formula. Independent direct-rule and coefficient/bitstring enumeration agree at every tested length 3–19; finite tests are not used in place of the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The canonical wheel couples local voting to a universal hub, producing a natural, nontrivial exact infinite-family cycle-population problem. The result separates globally oscillating hub-flip cycles from two exceptional constant-hub cycles and converts the former into a precise two-variable cyclic-run enumeration. The exact classification gives meaningful invariants not implied by the classical eventual period-two theorem.
